architecture_binding.target_scope: recipient-scoped OFFERED/DELIVERED/UPTAKEN evidence plus matched intervention/control causal falsification

candidate.name: EconML
candidate.observed_purpose: Machine-learning/econometrics toolkit for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects, including observational-data estimators, inference/confidence intervals, orthogonal learning, cross-fitting, causal forests and meta-learners.

source_observations: The core causal object is treatment T -> outcome Y conditioned on features/confounders X,W, with optional instruments Z for some estimators; causal interpretation depends on estimator-specific identification assumptions.
Orthogonal learners estimate nuisance functions and use cross-fitting with disjoint train/test folds before fitting the final heterogeneous treatment-effect model.
The package emphasizes aggregate/statistical effect estimation and uncertainty intervals rather than per-event deterministic causal receipts.

The 0.17.0 package has a broad scientific dependency surface including numpy, numba, scipy, scikit-learn, sparse, joblib, statsmodels, pandas, shap and lightgbm, with optional DoWhy and Ray integrations.

useful_thin_concepts: TREATMENT_OUTCOME_COVARIATE_SEPARATION: explicitly distinguish intervention assignment, measured downstream outcome and pre-treatment/context covariates.
CROSSFIT_STYLE_SEPARATION: keep estimator/model-selection data separate from held-out causal-effect evaluation to reduce researcher/test overfit when many WP507 experiments accumulate.

HETEROGENEOUS_EFFECT_CHARACTERIZATION: after exact per-run F2 receipts exist, analyze whether intervention effects vary by recipient, scenario, state or GRID context rather than assuming one global effect.
UNCERTAINTY_INTERVALS: preserve statistical uncertainty for aggregate effect estimates instead of converting noisy repeated-run differences into categorical causal truth.
NUISANCE_MODEL_EXPLICITNESS: if later observational covariates are used, make confounder/nuisance assumptions explicit and separately testable.
nontransferable_authority: An EconML ATE/CATE estimate cannot mint OFFERED, DELIVERED, UPTAKEN or causal-influence truth for a particular WP507 recipient/run.
Confidence intervals do not replace exact F2 broadcast/probe/recipient/selection/plan/cell provenance.
Observational causal identification assumptions are not evidence that F2 software-level matched intervention/control execution occurred correctly.
EconML artifacts/models must not become UnifiedDB canonical state, EffectGate authority, completion authority or a second truth store.
strongest_later_fit: F2-WP-902 whole-system characterization over repeated pre-registered causal experiments
F2-WP-806 lesion/rescue characterization where repeated noisy outcomes and heterogeneity require statistical aggregation
F2-WP-507 only as an optional aggregate-analysis layer after deterministic per-run causal receipts exist

counterhypothesis.statement: Repeated GWT intervention/control experiments may be noisy and heterogeneous enough that simple paired differences are insufficient; a CATE/DML-style estimator could improve calibration and reveal recipient/state-specific causal effects.
counterhypothesis.falsifier: Under a separately claimed no-real-effect experiment, compare a simple F2-native paired estimator against a pinned EconML estimator on synthetic/replayed data with known heterogeneous effects and injected confounding. Reject EconML if it adds no material calibration/heterogeneity benefit or if dependency/runtime/provenance cost outweighs the gain.

adjudication.reason: EconML is a statistical causal-estimation framework at a different causal layer from WP507's current deterministic per-recipient receipt contract. Its best current value is methodology distillation for later aggregate characterization, not core import.
